content.value_statement: Writers need structured scenes for an alien archaeology chapter. This skill supplies staged prompts, ethical dilemmas, and ending branches for Stella on Gaia.
actual_capabilities: Frames Stella Chen as the viewpoint character for an ancient ruins chapter.
Provides five staged exploration beats from entrance vista to reflective ending.
Offers discoveries about Eos history, crystal technology, and Gaia consciousness.
Defines three ending branches for archaeology, technology, and revelation outcomes.
Gives writing guidance for archaeology, civilization design, ethics, and mystery.
limitations: It is a narrative prompt, not a game engine or rules simulator.
Most source text mixes Chinese and English, so style may need localization.
It does not include executable tools, assets, maps, or validation logic.
It assumes the Stella, Gaia, and Eos story setting.

use_cases.title: Draft an Alien Archaeology Scene
use_cases.description: Create a guided ruins exploration chapter with visual discovery, historical clues, and Stella's internal reactions.

use_cases.title: Design a Choice-Driven Chapter
use_cases.description: Build decisions around sacred technology, Eos trust, and the cost of taking knowledge from Gaia.

use_cases.title: Run a Science Fiction Session
use_cases.description: Use the staged beats to guide players through mystery, wonder, danger, and ethical reflection.

prompt_templates.title: Begin the Ruins Approach
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to write Stella's first view of the ancient city. Emphasize awe, scale, and archaeological curiosity.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for the opening exploration scene

prompt_templates.title: Decode the Central Mural
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a scene where Stella studies the plaza mosaic and reconstructs the rise and fall of Eos civilization.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate history reveal through environmental storytelling

prompt_templates.title: Stage the Crystal Dilemma
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an interactive choice where Stella can take the central crystal or respect Eos warnings. Show consequences for both paths.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced ethical decision with branching outcomes

prompt_templates.title: Adapt the Full Chapter Arc
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert the five phases into a complete interactive fiction outline with pacing notes, emotional beats, and three endings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced adaptation for a larger narrative project

output_examples.input: Start the ruins chapter with Stella arriving alone.
output_examples.output: Stella reaches the city edge and sees crystal-lit streets under heavy vegetation. Her scanner records the scene while she asks where to begin.

output_examples.input: Reveal what happened to the Eos civilization.
output_examples.output: The plaza mosaic shows discovery, expansion, stellar disaster, and survival. Stella connects the images to the living Eos she has met.

output_examples.input: Write the ethical climax around the central crystal.
output_examples.output: Stella reaches for the crystal, then stops when Eos warns her. The scene shifts from extraction to shared knowledge and respect.

best_practices: Keep Stella's observations grounded in artifacts, murals, and environmental clues.
Reveal Eos history gradually through discoveries and dialogue.
Treat knowledge extraction as an ethical choice, not only a reward.
anti_patterns: Do not turn the ruins into a simple loot location.
Do not explain every mystery before the player can interpret it.
Do not ignore Eos agency when handling sacred technology.

faq.question: What kind of skill is this?
faq.answer: It is a narrative writing skill for an interactive science fiction chapter.

faq.question: Who is the main character?
faq.answer: The skill centers on Stella Chen as she explores ancient ruins on Gaia.

faq.question: Does it run code or tools?
faq.answer: No. The source contains story guidance and Markdown examples only.

faq.question: Can I use it without the earlier chapters?
faq.answer: Yes, but it works best when Stella, Gaia, and Eos are already established.

faq.question: What themes does it support?
faq.answer: It supports archaeology, lost civilization, responsible discovery, cultural respect, and planetary mystery.

faq.question: Can it support branching choices?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes archaeology, technology, and revelation endings for different player choices.
